scenario: Alterion 系统设计面，问推荐服务突然变慢会不会拖垮下单。你想说非核心功能先降级、保住主流程能走，但上次说成 "we just turn off some some features I guess" 就卡住了。
scenario_en: In an Alterion system-design round you're asked whether a slow recommendation service should drag down checkout. Last time you stalled at "we just turn off some some features I guess."
q: 想表达「非核心功能先降级、保住主流程可用」，该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "we degrade non-critical features first so the core flow stays up" out loud?
options: We degrade gracefully — turn off recommendations, but checkout keeps working.
We just turn off some some features I guess, so the important thing still work maybe.
So so if something's slow, we we kind of turn off, turn off some stuff, and the main thing, the main thing still runs...
Non-essential functional components shall be selectively disabled in order to preserve the availability of the primary transactional pathway.
tradeoff: 地道术语 graceful degradation + 具体例子 vs 大白话「turn off some features」：前者点名策略并给出真实取舍，后者听不出你有章法。
why: 术语是 graceful degradation：主动关掉非核心功能，保住核心流程可用。举一个具体例子（推荐 vs 下单）比抽象说 "turn off features" 更让人信服。
why_en: It's graceful degradation — turn off a non-critical piece like recommendations so the core flow, checkout, keeps working.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有功能都是核心、砍不掉任何一块，就该转向 "we'd rather shed load evenly" 而不是挑功能降级。
options_en: We degrade gracefully — turn off recommendations, but checkout keeps working.
We just turn off some some features I guess, so the important thing still work maybe.
So so if something's slow, we we kind of turn off, turn off some stuff, and the main thing, the main thing still runs...
Non-essential functional components shall be selectively disabled in order to preserve the availability of the primary transactional pathway.
optionMeanings: 地道：命名这个降级策略，配具体例子。
大白话「some some features」，没有术语没有例子。
反复 “so so / turn off” 打转，半天没落地。
shall be selectively disabled 书面腔，像念规范。
optionMeanings_en: Idiomatic: names the strategy with a concrete example.
Plain "some some features," no term, no example.
Loops on "so so / turn off," never lands.
"Shall be selectively disabled" — reads like a spec.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方立刻懂你有章法地保核心、丢边缘。
对方听不出你怎么挑该关的功能。
对方还在等你说清哪个留哪个关。
过度正式，像背文档不像设计对话。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They instantly see you'd deliberately keep the core, drop the edge.
They can't tell how you'd pick what to turn off.
They're still waiting for which piece stays and which goes.
Over-formal — reads like a spec, not a design chat.
optionDirectness: 抓住术语加具体例子的落点。
错在含糊，没有术语也没指哪个功能。
错在打转，主流程该怎么保住被口水句盖掉。
错在语域，书面体听着僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Nails the term plus a concrete example.
Wrong: vague, no term, no named feature.
Wrong because looping buries which flow gets kept.
Wrong register — written style feels stiff spoken.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统压力大或依赖出问题时，主动关掉非核心功能，保住核心流程能继续用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graceful degradation means deliberately turning off non-critical features under stress so the core flow keeps working.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户完成关键任务（如下单、支付）必须走通的那条主流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The core flow (critical path) is the sequence a user must complete for the key task, like checkout or payment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关掉也不影响核心任务完成的功能，比如推荐、个性化展示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A non-critical feature is one you can disable without blocking the core task, like recommendations or personalization.

scenario: Majestic Labs 系统设计面，问高负载下慢请求怎么办。你上次绕进 "the latency for the latency"、"we still have the latency" 的循环，没点出术语。
scenario_en: In a Majestic Labs system-design round you're asked about slow requests under load. Last time you looped on "the latency for the latency" and never named the term.
q: 想说「高负载下 p99 尾延迟飙升」，该怎么开口？
q_en: How do you say "p99 tail latency spikes under load" cleanly?
options: so the latency, the latency for the latency gets worse, the slow ones get slow when there's traffic...
Under the big load, the latency of the ninety-nine percent slowest requests becomes very high suddenly.
the slowest requests start to lag once traffic goes up, the tail end kind of gets bad over time.
Our p99 tail latency spikes under load, so I'd add a cache and shed load.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 复读打转："p99 tail latency spikes" 一句点名指标；"the latency for the latency" 是空转，暴露你没抓住尾延迟这个词。
why: 术语是 "p99 tail latency"——第 99 百分位的尾部延迟。带上负载触发和一个应对（cache / shed load），就把打转变成一句有指标的判断。
why_en: It's p99 tail latency — say "spikes under load" plus a fix like cache or shed load, and the loop becomes one metric-anchored line.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官只关心平均体验、没追问尾部，直接说 "latency goes up under load" 就够，不必上 p99。
options_en: so the latency, the latency for the latency gets worse, the slow ones get slow when there's traffic...
Under the big load, the latency of the ninety-nine percent slowest requests becomes very high suddenly.
the slowest requests start to lag once traffic goes up, the tail end kind of gets bad over time.
Our p99 tail latency spikes under load, so I'd add a cache and shed load.
optionMeanings: 空转打转，反复说慢却没术语。
把 p99 硬翻成 ninety-nine percent，直译腔。
只说 tail end gets bad，没量化没应对。
点名指标 + 负载触发 + 一个具体应对。
optionMeanings_en: Spins in place, all slow, never a term.
Translates p99 as "ninety-nine percent" — calque.
Just "tail end gets bad," no number, no fix.
Names the metric, the trigger, and one fix.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听出你在原地绕，没锁定问题。
能懂，但一听就是逐字翻译。
对方不知你会怎么量、怎么救。
一句给出指标、诱因、方向，显老练。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hear you circling, never pinning it.
Clear, but obviously word-for-word.
They don't know how you'd measure or fix it.
One line: metric, trigger, direction — seasoned.
optionDirectness: 错在复读打转，零信息。
错在直译，那不是英语说法。
错在含糊，没指标也没应对动作。
抓住尾延迟飙升加一个具体缓解。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: pure loop, says nothing.
Wrong: a calque, not how it's said.
Wrong: vague, no metric and no action.
Nails the tail-latency spike plus a mitigation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位延迟：把请求延迟排序后第 99% 那个值，代表大多数用户里最慢的一批体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 is the 99th-percentile latency — the value below which 99% of requests fall, capturing the slow tail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 尾延迟：延迟分布尾部（最慢那批请求）的延迟，常用 p99/p999 衡量，比平均更影响体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tail latency is the latency of the slowest requests in the distribution, usually measured at p99 or p999.

termDefinitions.meaning: 卸载/丢负载：过载时主动拒绝或降级一部分请求，保住其余请求的延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To shed load is to drop or reject some requests under overload so the rest stay fast.

scenario: Gamma 后端面，问你的系统怎么扩容。你上次反复说 "large scale system"、"the scaling scale of the system"，没落到具体机制。
scenario_en: In a Gamma backend round you're asked how your system scales. Last time you repeated "large scale system" and "the scaling scale of the system" without a mechanism.
q: 想说「加无状态节点、水平扩容抗流量」，该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "scale out with stateless nodes to handle traffic" out loud?
options: We scale out horizontally — add stateless nodes behind the load balancer as traffic grows.
We make the system bigger to handle more scale, so it can take the large scale of the traffic.
So for scaling, the scale, we add more of the things, more servers I mean, so it handles more.
The system shall be scaled along the horizontal dimension via provisioning of additional server nodes.
tradeoff: 地道动词形 vs 名词打转："scale out horizontally" 是动作 + 机制；"the scaling scale of the system" 只是名词绕圈，没说你到底怎么扩。
why: 用动词 "scale out horizontally"，再配无状态节点和负载均衡才说清机制：无状态才能随便加机、由 LB 分流。名词堆 "scale" 是空转。
why_en: Say the verb "scale out horizontally," then "stateless nodes behind the load balancer" — that's the mechanism, not a pile of the noun "scale."
whenOtherWins: 如果瓶颈是单机 CPU/内存、加机器无用，就该说 "scale up"（纵向扩），而不是 scale out。
options_en: We scale out horizontally — add stateless nodes behind the load balancer as traffic grows.
We make the system bigger to handle more scale, so it can take the large scale of the traffic.
So for scaling, the scale, we add more of the things, more servers I mean, so it handles more.
The system shall be scaled along the horizontal dimension via provisioning of additional server nodes.
optionMeanings: 动词加无状态节点加 LB，机制齐全。
make it bigger 名词堆，没说怎么扩。
打转半天才补上 servers。
along the horizontal dimension 书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Verb plus stateless nodes and the load balancer.
"Make it bigger" — noun pile, no mechanism.
Loops before finally reaching "servers."
"Along the horizontal dimension" — a spec sheet.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方立刻懂你要横向加无状态实例。
对方只听到「更大」，不知怎么做。
对方等半天才等到 servers。
过度正式，像背文档不像聊设计。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They immediately get horizontal stateless replicas.
They hear only "bigger," not what you'd do.
They wait through the loop for "servers."
Over-formal — reciting a doc, not designing.
optionDirectness: 抓住动词加无状态加 LB 的落点。
错在名词堆，没动作也没机制。
错在打转，迟迟不落地。
错在语域，书面体听着别扭。
optionDirectness_en: Nails the verb plus stateless plus LB.
Wrong: noun pile, no action, no mechanism.
Wrong: loops, lands too late.
Wrong register — written style feels off.

termDefinitions.meaning: 横向扩容：靠加更多机器/实例来提升容量，对应 scale up（纵向，换更强的单机）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To scale out is to add more machines to grow capacity, as opposed to scaling up a single stronger box.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无状态：节点自己不保存会话/数据，任何一台都能处理任意请求，所以可随意增删。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stateless node keeps no local session or data, so any node can serve any request and you can add or remove them freely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载均衡器：把进来的流量分发到后面多台节点，常缩写 LB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer spreads incoming traffic across the pool of backend nodes.

scenario: 系统设计面，问下游依赖挂了怎么避免雪崩。你想说熔断，但怕术语的搭配说错。
scenario_en: In a system-design round you're asked how to stop a dead dependency from cascading. You want to say "circuit breaker" but fear botching the collocation.
q: 想说「连续失败后熔断打开，停止打死掉的下游」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "the circuit breaker trips open after repeated failures and stops calling the dead dependency"?
options: when the other service is down, we just stop calling it for a while so it can recover somehow.
we open a circuit breaker to break the circuit when the calls are failing too much time.
The circuit breaker trips open after N failures, so we stop hammering a dead dependency.
so if it keeps failing, we sort of cut it off, we stop the calls, then later we try it again maybe.
tradeoff: 地道搭配 vs 生造搭配："trips open" 是熔断器的标准说法；"break the circuit ... too much time" 是硬凑，暴露你只听过词、没用过。
why: 标准搭配是 "the circuit breaker trips open"，不是 open/break a circuit。加一句停止打死掉的下游，就点出机制：连续失败后快速失败。
why_en: The collocation is "the circuit breaker trips open" — then "stop hammering a dead dependency" shows the mechanism: fail fast instead of pounding a dead service.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是偶发的一次失败、下游没挂，直接 retry 就行，不必上熔断这套。
options_en: when the other service is down, we just stop calling it for a while so it can recover somehow.
we open a circuit breaker to break the circuit when the calls are failing too much time.
The circuit breaker trips open after N failures, so we stop hammering a dead dependency.
so if it keeps failing, we sort of cut it off, we stop the calls, then later we try it again maybe.
optionMeanings: 描述了行为却没术语，somehow 收尾没底。
说了熔断器，但动词搭配全错。
标准搭配加阈值加停止打下游。
sort of cut it off 打转，机制含糊。
optionMeanings_en: Describes behavior but no term; "somehow" sounds unsure.
Says circuit breaker but the collocation is off.
Standard phrasing plus threshold and stopping the call.
"Sort of cut it off" loop, mechanism stays fuzzy.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方懂大意，但觉得你没有现成词。
术语在，搭配错让人疑你没真用过。
对方立刻认出这是熔断的标准表达。
对方仍不确定触发条件和动作。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They get the gist but sense you lack vocabulary.
Term's there, but wrong collocation raises doubt.
They instantly recognize standard circuit-breaker phrasing.
They still can't tell the trigger or the action.
optionDirectness: 错在没术语，靠 somehow 兜显得不熟。
错在搭配，破电路那句太生硬。
抓住标准搭配加阈值加快速失败。
错在打转，sort of 让机制说不清。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: no term, leans on "somehow," unpracticed.
Wrong collocation: "break the circuit" is clumsy.
Nails the standard phrasing plus threshold and fail-fast.
Wrong: loops on "sort of," mechanism unclear.

termDefinitions.meaning: 熔断器：一种容错模式，某依赖连续失败超过阈值就「打开」，短路后续调用，直接快速失败，给下游喘息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker is a fault-tolerance pattern that stops calling a failing dependency once errors cross a threshold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 熔断跳开：熔断器从闭合（正常放行）切到打开（拦截调用）的动作，是它的标准动词搭配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: "Trips open" is the standard phrase for a circuit breaker switching from closed to open and blocking calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依赖：你的服务要调用的下游服务或组件，它挂了会拖累你。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dependency is a downstream service your code calls; if it fails, it can drag you down too.

scenario: WOP.com 支付方向面，问重试导致重复扣款怎么办。你想说幂等 + 退避重试，但怕说成口水话。
scenario_en: In a WOP.com payments round you're asked how to stop retries from double-charging. You want to say idempotent plus backoff without turning it into mush.
q: 想说「重试加指数退避，并做成幂等，双重提交变成无操作」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "retry with exponential backoff and make it idempotent so a double-submit is a no-op"?
options: we retry it again, and we make it so the retry doesn't do it twice by accident, like a double charge.
so we try again, and then again, and we wait a bit each time, and we make sure it doesn't, um, double.
The retry mechanism shall be rendered idempotent such that duplicate submissions produce no effect at all.
We retry with exponential backoff and make it idempotent, so a double-submit is a no-op.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 绕圈解释："idempotent ... a no-op" 一句到位；"doesn't do it twice by accident" 是在绕着解释幂等，暴露你没这个词。
why: 术语是 "idempotent" 和 "exponential backoff"，收尾用无操作证明你懂机制：重试安全、退避不打垮下游，而不是用大白话绕。
why_en: Say "idempotent" and "exponential backoff," close with "a double-submit is a no-op" — the term proves the mechanism instead of talking around it.
whenOtherWins: 如果操作本身就只读、无副作用，直接 retry 即可，不必强调幂等或退避。
options_en: we retry it again, and we make it so the retry doesn't do it twice by accident, like a double charge.
so we try again, and then again, and we wait a bit each time, and we make sure it doesn't, um, double.
The retry mechanism shall be rendered idempotent such that duplicate submissions produce no effect at all.
We retry with exponential backoff and make it idempotent, so a double-submit is a no-op.
optionMeanings: 用大白话绕着解释，就是不说术语。
try again and again 口水话，没术语。
术语对但 shall be rendered 太书面。
退避加幂等加无操作，全齐。
optionMeanings_en: Talks around it in plain words, never the term.
"Try again and again" — mush, no term.
Right term but "shall be rendered" too stiff.
Backoff plus idempotent plus no-op, all in.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方懂你意思，但觉得你缺这个词。
对方听半天没听到任何术语。
术语在，但腔调像念规范文档。
支付面试官一听就知你真做过安全重试。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They follow you but sense you lack the word.
They wait through it, hear no term at all.
Term's there, but reads like a spec doc.
A payments interviewer knows you've built safe retries.
optionDirectness: 错在绕圈解释，没说出幂等。
错在口水话，退避和幂等都没点名。
错在语域，那句太书面。
抓住退避加幂等加无操作的落点。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: talks around it, never "idempotent."
Wrong: mush; neither backoff nor idempotency named.
Wrong register: too written.
Nails backoff, idempotent, and the no-op anchor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等：同一操作执行一次和执行多次结果一样，所以重试或重复提交不会造成二次副作用（如重复扣款）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation has the same effect whether it runs once or many times, so retries can't double-charge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指数退避：每次重试等待时间成倍增长（如 1s、2s、4s），避免失败时一拥而上把下游压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exponential backoff doubles the wait between retries so a struggling dependency isn't hammered by a retry storm.

termDefinitions.meaning: 空操作：一次不产生任何效果的调用；幂等下的重复提交就变成 no-op。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A no-op is a call that has no effect; under idempotency a duplicate submit becomes a no-op.

scenario: Gamma 后端面，问一个分片挂了会不会拖垮整个集群。你想说「把它隔离开，爆炸半径只到一个分片，不会波及整个 fleet」，但 blast radius 这个词想不起来，说成 “it doesn't spread to like everything, hopefully”。
scenario_en: In a Gamma backend round you're asked whether one bad shard takes down the whole cluster. You want to say you isolate it so the blast radius is one shard, not the whole fleet, but the term won't come and it comes out as "it doesn't spread to like everything, hopefully."
q: 想说「把故障隔离开，爆炸半径只限一个分片，不会波及整个 fleet」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "we isolate it so the blast radius is one shard, not the whole fleet"?
options: It doesn't spread to like everything, hopefully, because we kind of keep it in its own place.
So so if one shard, one shard breaks, it it stays there, it doesn't go, doesn't go to the other ones, I think...
Fault isolation mechanisms are implemented such that the scope of impact is confined to a singular partition.
We isolate it so the blast radius is one shard, not the whole fleet.
tradeoff: 地道术语 blast radius vs 含糊「hopefully it doesn't spread」：前者一句话点名隔离范围，后者听着像在祈祷而不是设计。
why: 术语是 blast radius：一次故障最多能波及的范围。配一句「只限一个分片、不波及整个 fleet」，就点出隔离的边界在哪。
why_en: The term is blast radius — the scope one failure can reach. Pairing it with "one shard, not the whole fleet" names the isolation boundary.
whenOtherWins: 如果分片强耦合、隔离不了，就该说 "it could still ripple"，别硬套 blast radius。
options_en: It doesn't spread to like everything, hopefully, because we kind of keep it in its own place.
So so if one shard, one shard breaks, it it stays there, it doesn't go, doesn't go to the other ones, I think...
Fault isolation mechanisms are implemented such that the scope of impact is confined to a singular partition.
We isolate it so the blast radius is one shard, not the whole fleet.
optionMeanings: 「hopefully」暴露没有把握，也没有术语。
反复 “so so / doesn't go doesn't go” 打转，没收尾。
「mechanisms are implemented such that」书面腔念定义。
blast radius 命名边界，一分片对整个 fleet。
optionMeanings_en: "Hopefully" gives away the uncertainty, and no term.
Loops on "so so / doesn't go doesn't go," never lands.
A stiff "mechanisms are implemented such that" reading.
Names blast radius: one shard versus the whole fleet.
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官听出你没把握，像是在赌运气。
对方还没听清故障到底会不会扩散。
太正式，像读规范不像讲设计。
一句话点出隔离边界，面试官立刻放心。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer hears you gambling, not designing.
They still can't tell if the failure actually spreads.
Too formal — sounds like a spec, not design talk.
One line names the isolation boundary; they're reassured.
optionDirectness: 错在含糊，「hopefully」不是设计判断。
错在打转，隔离边界被口水句盖掉。
错在语域：口语场合用书面体显僵硬。
抓住 blast radius + 一分片对 fleet 的落点。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: vague, "hopefully" isn't a design decision.
Wrong because looping buries the isolation boundary.
Wrong register — written style feels stiff spoken.
Nails blast radius plus the one-shard-vs-fleet anchor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 爆炸半径：一次故障最多能波及到的范围，范围越小说明隔离做得越好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blast radius is the scope a single failure can reach; a smaller radius means better isolation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把故障限制在一个组件或分片内，不让它蔓延到其他部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To isolate a failure is to contain it to one component or shard so it can't spread further.

termDefinitions.meaning: 舱壁模式：把资源（连接池、线程池）按组件分开，一个组件耗尽资源不会拖垮其他组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The bulkhead pattern partitions resources like connection or thread pools per component, so one exhausting its pool doesn't sink the rest.
